types/utils.ts/Overwrite: only overwrite keys of objects

Overwrite<string,string> resulted in a mangled object type
because the existing implementation iterated over the string
type's keys (e.g. 'charCodeAt')

This commit changes the implementation so that keys are only
iterated and overwritten in the case of objects. Otherwise,
a non-never TWith type will entirely replace TType, e.g.
Overwrite<string, number> results in 'number'.

summary.intent: Fix inferred input types for procedures that combine .input() with .use() by making Overwrite replace non-object types instead of mangling them (commit 7dc04a7; PR body is an unfilled template).
summary.issue_fit: Issue alignment unavailable (no linked issue); intent taken from the PR title and commit 7dc04a7. The reported input case is fixed, but the same Overwrite change regresses next({ ctx }) typing.

findings.title: Keep the previous context when next() gets a non-object ctx
findings.trigger: A middleware calls `opts.next({ ctx: maybe })` with `maybe: { extra: number } | undefined`, and a later resolver reads `ctx.base` from the root context.
findings.impact: The new `Overwrite` returns the non-object `TWith`, so ctx becomes possibly `undefined` and the resolver fails with TS18048, although `next()` spreads `{ ...callOpts.ctx, ...nextOpts.ctx }` and never drops the previous context; the merge-base type kept it.
findings.change: Leave the shared `Overwrite` as is, since the input fix depends on it, and in `packages/server/src/core/internals/procedureBuilder.ts` (and the matching `_ctx_out` merges in `middleware.ts`) use a ctx-specific merge that keeps `TType` when `TWith` is `undefined` or `null`. Add a regression test for `next({ ctx: obj | undefined })`.
findings.source: Commit 7dc04a7 body, "a non-never TWith type will entirely replace TType"; released contract of `next({ ctx })` at @trpc/server 10.43.2.

observations.fact: The doc comment says a non-object `TType` is replaced by `TWith` "unless TWith is never", but the trailing `: TType` branch is unreachable because `TWith extends any` distributes over `never` and yields `never`.
observations.evidence: `packages/server/src/core/internals/utils.ts:25-30`; scratch check: `Overwrite<string, never>` is `never`, as at the merge-base.

observations.fact: The regression test declares `voidWithMiddleware` but never asserts on it, and leaves `// ^?` twoslash markers in place.
